title: What is known about 1RB0RA_1RC0RF_1RD1LE_1RE---_1LF1LE_1RA0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_1RC0RF_1RD1LE_1RE---_1LF1LE_1RA0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. With a = 10 and b = 110, the tape at the extensions is a list of blocks a^x separated by 0, 0^3, b or 1^2 b. At step 9,866,788,243 there are 453 blocks; the largest are 26719, 6670, 6669, 3334, 1683, 823 (each about half the one before), and 377 of them are shorter than 20. The width grows like 1.14·√t. The sweeps are proved in Lean; the block rule is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 36,489 cells have been visited and 18,333 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.518). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.148).

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text:
The head sweeps over long runs of a repeated word, rewriting each copy, for any number n of copies and any surrounding tape. Examples:
  • L (01)^n E> 0 R → L E> 0 (01)^n R
  • L (10)^n F> 1 R → L F> 1 (10)^n R
  • L (1010101)^n F> 1 R → L F> 1 (1010110)^n R
  • L A> (10101)^n R → L (01010)^n A> R
Generated by py/rules.py (tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py).

claims.title: Halving block sizes
claims.text: At the 560 extensions up to step 1010 (tools/c/tokrun, a = 10, b = 110), the large blocks at the left come in a roughly halving sequence that grows slowly: 26310, 6565, 6565, 3282, 1658, 814 at step 9,566,602,752 and 26719, 6670, 6669, 3334, 1683, 823 at step 9,866,788,243.

claims.title: Square-root width
claims.text: The width (rightmost minus leftmost visited cell) is 32,845 at step 8.0·10<sup>8</sup> and 112,986 at step 9.87·10<sup>9</sup>, about 1.14·√t; the number of blocks grows from 171 to 453 over the same range.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LC_1RC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LC_1RF0RE_1RA0RD up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 36,489 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Hundreds of blocks
html:
Write a for 10 and b for 110. At step 9,866,788,243 the tape starts

E> 0 a^6 b a^26719 b a^3 b a^6 b a^6670 0 a^10 0 a^6669 b a^4 b a^18 0 a^3334 0 a^7 b a^43 1^2 b a^1683 ...

and goes on for 453 blocks; the right part is a long stretch of small blocks (3, 4, 5, ...). The large blocks roughly halve from one to the next, which suggests a binary counter whose digits are block sizes, but the small blocks between them change on every sweep and no rule has been found.

sections.heading: Slow growth
html: The width grows like 1.14·√t, the number of blocks grows (171 at step 8·108, 453 at 1010), and the large blocks grow by a few hundred per 3·108 steps. A halt (D reading 1) has not occurred in 1010 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.518). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.148).
After 109 steps the tape spans 36,489 cells (24,600 left of the start, 2,294 right), with a density of 1s of 0.502.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1LC_1RC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LC_1RF0RE_1RA0RD: rename A→E, B→F, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→D; it is this table started in state C

summary: A tape of hundreds of blocks of pairs 10 separated by short separators (0, 000, 110, 11 110). A few large blocks at the left roughly halve in size from one to the next (26719, 6670, 6669, 3334, 1683, 823, ...); hundreds of small ones fill the right. The width grows like the square root of the step count. Counter-like, not understood; halting open.
